name: Todo Sushi
blocked: needs-browser: restaurant's own site (todosushisd.com) is a Wix site whose /menu and /menu2 pages are fully client-rendered with zero prices, zero JSON-LD, and no data-hook=item.price spans anywhere in the static HTML -- confirmed by stripping tags and by grepping for a 'price' JSON key (0 hits). No menu PDF or photo found on the site either. Both delivery platforms ARE reachable and agree closely: DoorDash marketplace (doordash.com/store/todo-sushi-san-diego-26324295/, address-confirmed 9823 Carroll Canyon Road) gave 91 items across 9 sections via schema.org Menu JSON-LD; Uber Eats (ubereats.com/store/todo-sushi/..., address 9823 Carroll Canyon Rd) gave a fuller 171 items across 16 sections (adds Nigiri, Sashimi Specials, Maki Cut Rolls, House Special Rolls, Chef Specials, Bento Box, Lunch specials) via __REACT_QUERY_STATE__ -> catalogSectionsMap (integer-cent prices; the standard \u0022-unescape needed a second pass because the seoMeta.metaJson field is itself a percent-encoded nested JSON string whose escaped quotes are `%5C\u0022`, which the normal global unescape corrupts into a bare quote mid-string and breaks JSON.parse -- fixed by first converting `%5C\u0022` to a real escaped quote `\"` before the general unescape; noted here as a new technique). Overlapping items between the two platforms match to the cent (Edamame $5.85/$5.85, Special Edamame $11.64/$11.64, California Roll $13.26/$13.26, Shrimp Tempura Crunch Roll $18.72/$18.72), which per the playbook does NOT clear a markup on its own. Ran the markup test on the fuller 171-item Uber Eats set: dividing by 1.3 lands 163/171 prices on a clean nickel and 79/171 (46%) specifically on a $X.95 ending (Edamame 5.85/1.3=4.50, Salmon Skin Tempura 9.75/1.3=7.50, Chicken Karaage 15.54/1.3=11.954, etc.) -- a strong signature of a uniform ~30% markup baked into both delivery catalogs rather than the wall price, matching the Pacific Pizza precedent in the playbook (two ordering channels agreeing does not clear a markup). No dine-in artefact (photo, PDF, printed menu) was reachable by curl. Needs a browser to read the real Wix /menu and /menu2 tabs (both server-render only the active tab; the other needs a click) or to check Yelp's photo gallery for a dated menu photo.

name: Burritos Santana
blocked: needs-browser (or a dine-in artefact): identified this branch's own ordering platform -- santanasmexfood.com/locations/ lists 'Santana Burrito El cajon' at '533 El Cajon Blvd San Diego, CA 92115' (matches the work list's 5330 El Cajon Blvd, missing a trailing 0 in the site's own text) linking to https://burritossantana.smartonlineorder.com/, the Clover WordPress plugin (smartonlineorder.com is a new platform seen this batch: /wp-json/moo-clover/v1/categories then /categories/{uuid}/items, items nested under a top-level items[] array in the category object, integer cents). Pulled all 17 categories, 222 items. Ran the mandatory 4% markup test and it is unambiguous: dividing every price by 1.04 lands on a clean quarter-dollar 176/222 times (79%), and manually checking individual items shows exact wall-price landings with zero exceptions in the first 20 checked (Monster Burrito w/Drink $17.16 -> $16.50, Cabeza Burrito $14.56 -> $14.00, Chimichanga Burrito $15.34 -> $14.75, Grande Burrito $18.72 -> $18.00, etc.) -- a 4% online-ordering surcharge baked into the storefront, not the wall price. Per the non-negotiable rule against constructing a price, the divided-out base was NOT filed. No menu PDF, photo, or other channel (DoorDash/UberEats/Yelp) was checked yet for this specific location within the time budget; the site's homepage and locations page carry no menu PDF or photo link. Needs a browser to check Yelp's photo gallery for a dated menu photo of this location, or a delivery-platform listing for this exact address (533X El Cajon Blvd) as a cross-check. Note the same small chain operates 3 other San Diego-area smartonlineorder.com storefronts (burritossantana2, santanasmexfood) not checked here; per the sibling-branch rule, a menu found under one of those would not be filed under this restaurant's id without its own address confirmation.

name: Et Voilà! French Bistro
notes: Router said no-platform; restaurant's own WordPress site uses a custom menu plugin (h3.evm-section-title / ul.evm-items / li.evm-item with evm-item-title, evm-item-price, evm-item-desc), fully server-rendered and readable by plain curl on both /menu/food/ and /menu/drinks/. Address 3015 Adams confirmed on the homepage matching the work list. Prices on the page are bare numbers with no currency symbol (e.g. '18', '29'); '$' and '.00' added here since all are whole dollars. 'Ravioli aux champignons' is listed as two portion prices '18/28' (small/large) and is recorded as two dishes with the size noted in the name, not averaged or merged. The 'Fromages' row is a cheese-board ingredient list with no price at all (no size, no number) and was dropped per the no-price rule -- it reads as an unpriced adjunct description, not a missing number for an otherwise-priced item. On the drinks page, 'Beer' (Draft + Bottle) was kept as a real drink-menu section; 'Liquors' (Tequila/Vodka/Whiskey by brand, priced per pour with no description) is a back-bar spirits reference and was excluded as an adjunct per the playbook's explicit rule, not filed. 'Plateau de desserts' appears twice at two different prices ($14 whose description is a near-duplicate of Pêche Melba's, and $25 with its own dessert-platter description) -- recorded both exactly as printed on the site rather than resolved, since neither can be confirmed a typo without contacting the restaurant. 79 dishes across Appetizers, Main Courses, Mussels, Sides, Desserts (food) and Cocktails, Classic French apéritifs, Beer (drinks). None inferred, merged, divided, or truncated beyond what's noted.

name: WING LEGENDS & BOBA BLENDS
notes: Router said no-platform; restaurant's own Squarespace site's #menu-section embeds photographed screen-menu images explicitly filenamed '...SCREEN MENU...(NO PRICE)-01..05.jpg' -- confirmed literally priceless, so its own site could not be used. Found the restaurant on both DoorDash (doordash.com/store/wing-legends-san-diego-802411/, address-confirmed 1515 Palm Avenue) and Uber Eats (address-confirmed 1515 Palm Ave, San Diego, CA 92154), both matching the work list exactly. Filed from DoorDash (87 raw items across 18 sections incl. schema.org Menu JSON-LD); markup test found no consistent divisor (best was only 12/87 on 1.25), so no uniform surcharge detected. Dropped the 'Most Ordered' section entirely as a duplicate sample (all 12 of its items reappear in their proper categorized sections). DoorDash's own catalog carries internal data-quality problems handled as follows, none guessed: (1) several items are priced as an ambiguous 'X for $Y' promotional string rather than a plain per-item price (Buffalo Chicken Salad, Boba Specialties, Pulled Pork Rice Bowl) -- dropped, since 'for' pricing isn't a confirmed single-item number; (2) 'Pulled Pork Fries' appears twice in the Fries section with two different plain prices ($17.99 and $23.99) with no distinguishing name or description -- an unresolvable same-page disagreement, so both were dropped rather than guessing which is real; (3) 'Full Rack of Baby Back Ribs and 3 Sides' ($39.99) is listed identically under both 'Our Specialties' and 'Ribs' -- kept once. Cross-checked against Uber Eats (a different owner): item names mostly match but UBER EATS PRICES RUN CONSISTENTLY HIGHER on the same dishes (5 Traditional Wings $19.99 vs DoorDash $12.99; Buffalo Fries $23.99 vs $17.99; Mozzarella Sticks $14.99 vs $11.99; Legends Plate $28.99 vs $21.99; Family Combos $65.99+ vs $59.99+) -- not used to corroborate DoorDash's numbers, noted as a real per-platform pricing difference rather than a markup formula (no single divisor fit either full set). 66 dishes across Sandwich Combos, Fries, Our Specialties, Appetizers, Wings and Tenders, Personal Combos, Family Combos, Kids Meal, Salads, Sides, Desserts, Drinks (incl. Boba Blends/Refresher/Milk Tea -- the restaurant's namesake boba items are present), Special Rice Bowls, Crispy Wraps, Ribs, Fries Combos, Chicken Wraps. name: El Paisa
notes: Router flagged elpaisa.shop as no-platform. Checked against the playbook's brand-twin farm-domain warning for cheap-TLD name-based domains (<name>.shop etc that 301 to a different registrable domain with no prices) -- this domain does NOT match: curl -sIL shows no redirect at all (stays on elpaisa.shop, 200), and the site is a fully priced, real restaurant site (address 3096 National Ave confirmed on the homepage), so it was not treated as barred. The dedicated /menu page is plain server-rendered HTML (h2.heading--title section banners + h3.dish--title/span.dish--price dish-panels), readable by plain curl. IMPORTANT structural gotcha: the page alternates which side of each two-column row holds the section-title banner vs. the item list (left-image/right-items, then right-image/left-items, alternating), so a naive linear title-then-items regex misattributes many items to the wrong section (e.g. attributes Tacos-section items to Combinations, 0 items to Tacos). Fixed by splitting on each <section id="coverN">...</section> block first and pairing its one h2 with its own dish-panels regardless of left/right order. Markup test (divide by 1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25/1.3/0.96) found no divisor landing more than 12/93 on a quarter-dollar -- passes as ordinary POS-style pricing, not a surcharge. Three items (Rolled Tacos, Carne Asada Chips, Carne Asada Fries) have a genuinely empty price span in the raw markup (confirmed, not a parsing gap) and were dropped per the no-price rule. 93 dishes across all 15 of the site's own sections (Combinations, Tacos, Antojitos, Fries, Burros, Breakfast Burrito, Burros Nuevos, Breakfast Plates, Tortas, Caldos, Seafood, Extras, Kids Combo, Desserts, Beverages). None inferred, merged, or divided.

name: The Promiscuous Fork
notes: Router said no-platform; restaurant's own site links a plain old-style HTML menu.html (table/td layout, class=menu-cat section spans, class=testify description paragraphs), readable by plain curl. Address 6984 La Jolla Blvd confirmed on the site. IMPORTANT catch: roughly 60% of the raw page (Extras, Sides, Drinks, Give me Caffeine, a Brunch/Specials block explicitly headed 'Crown Point Location', a dedicated Tommy Want Wingy $9 wings section, a Sliders section, and several Burgers/Sammiches rows including Pot Roast Sandwich, Bacon Wrapped BBQ Shrimp Po' Boy, Caprese sandwich, Cubana and Mini Portobello Sliders) is wrapped in HTML <!-- --> comments and is NOT rendered on the live page at all -- confirmed by counting comment markers (16 open, 13 close, all of which paired up on a manual sequential scan with no unclosed comment) and by manually inspecting each block. The Brunch/Crown Point block is explicitly a different branch's menu and was excluded on that basis too. A first pass that did not strip comments would have filed 16 dead/wrong-branch rows as live; this was caught before filing anything. Also fixed two price-extraction traps in the live rows: 'Mac 'n Cheese' has its real price ($15) directly after the name with add-on prices ($7)/($6) parenthesized in the description afterward, while 'Pork Fried Rice' has its real price ($17) at the END of the description with a parenthesized add-on price ($2 for a fried egg) appearing earlier in the text -- solved generally by stripping all parenthesized amounts before picking the price, rather than assuming first-or-last. Markup test not applicable (no delivery platform involved, restaurant's own static page). 34 dishes across the sections that are actually live: Happy Hour (Dine-In Only), Fork'n Faves, Salads, Tacos, Bowls, Burgers, Sammiches, Food for the Kiddos. Checked and confirmed missing from the live page (no adjunct excluded, genuinely absent): a Drinks/Wine/Beer list, Sides, Extras -- these exist only in the disabled/commented content and could not be filed as current. None inferred, merged, or divided.

name: DJK Korean BBQ(Dae Jang Keum)
blocked: the listed website (djkkoreanbbq.com) is a parked domain -- its 200-OK response is a JS ad-redirect page loading router.parklogic.com (a domain-parking ad network), not the restaurant's real site; treated as a dead domain, not a hijack to another business. Found two DIFFERENT DoorDash marketplace listings for this exact restaurant, both address-confirmed at 7905 Engineer Road, San Diego (matching the work list): doordash.com/store/djk-korean-bbq-san-diego-926331/ (77 items, 10 sections, via schema.org Menu JSON-LD) and doordash.com/store/dae-jang-keum-korean-bbq-san-diego-62390/ (43 items, 6 sections). WebSearch independently reports both this restaurant's Uber Eats and DoorDash presence as currently inactive/closed for ordering, consistent with these being stale marketplace pages rather than a live storefront. The two DoorDash listings disagree sharply and consistently on matching items -- Bibimbap $25.08 vs $13.99, Yukgaejang $25.08 vs $14.99, Galbi Tang $32.97 vs $17.99, Doenjang Jjigae $22.33 vs $12.99, Pork Belly (Samgyeopsal) $47.48 vs $26.99 (Sam Kyp Sal) -- a consistent ~1.75-1.83x gap with no single clean divisor found in the markup test on either set (best hit was only 8/77 and 6/43 on any tested divisor, not the near-total match a real markup leaves). Per the playbook, a 2x-scale disagreement between sources on the same dish means what is visible is unreliable, not a small true sample -- blocked rather than filing either number as a partial. Neither listing's prices were filed. Needs a browser to check which DoorDash listing (if either) reflects current dine-in pricing, or to read Yelp/Facebook photos of a physical menu.
